# Cris Santos Company | Energy | Micro: Small intrastate pipeline

> Cris Santos Company, LLC is a micro business with 7 employees, operating as a small intrastate pipeline.

This folder is a self-contained scenario. Read this page first, then open the project folders in step order (step-01 to step-10). Each project folder has a `_context.md` explaining what that deliverable looks like for this company.

> **Completed sample.** All 10 deliverables in this folder are filled in. The detailed company facts they share (locations, systems, current security posture) are in [00_company-facts.md](00_company-facts.md). Read it second.

## What the business handles
- **Sensitive data:** CEII (18 CFR 388.113); BES Cyber System Information (CIP-011); SSI (49 CFR Part 1520) - TSA SD content and pipeline security info; Customer PII/usage data
- **Critical systems:** EMS/SCADA; ICCP links; Substation automation and protective relays; Generation DCS; Pipeline SCADA, compressor/pump station PLCs; LNG terminal DCS/SIS; Physical access control systems (PACS) and EACMS

## Who regulates it
SRMA: Department of Energy (DOE); FERC; NERC and Regional Entities; TSA (pipeline/LNG security); PHMSA (pipeline safety incl. SCADA control room management)

| Requirement | Citation | Size thresholds / exemptions |
|---|---|---|
| [NERC CIP Reliability Standards (CIP-002 through CIP-014; CIP-015 approved)](https://www.nerc.com/standards/reliability-standards/cip) | Federal Power Act sec. 215 (16 U.S.C. 824o); 18 CFR Part 40; NERC CIP-002-5.1a, CIP-003-9, CIP-004 to CIP-014 (current enforceable versions) | Impact rating via CIP-002 Attachment 1 bright-line criteria, e.g., medium impact for generation with net Real Power capability >= 1,500 MW in a single Interconnection; high impact for control centers of BA/GOP/TOP controlling >= 3,000 MW; UFLS/UVLS programs of 300 MW or more bring Distribution Providers into scope. Low-impact assets have reduced (CIP-003) requirements. |
| [TSA Security Directive Pipeline-2021-01G (Enhancing Pipeline Cybersecurity)](https://www.tsa.gov/sites/default/files/signed_security-directive-pipeline-2021-01g-and-transmittal-memo_508c.pdf) | TSA SD Pipeline-2021-01G, issued under 49 U.S.C. 114 | No numeric threshold; applies only to systems/facilities TSA has notified as critical. |
| [TSA Security Directive Pipeline-2021-02G (Pipeline Cybersecurity Mitigation Actions, Contingency Planning, and Testing)](https://www.tsa.gov/sites/default/files/signed_security_directive_pipeline-2021-02g_and_transmittal_memo_508c.pdf) | TSA SD Pipeline-2021-02G, issued under 49 U.S.C. 114 | No numeric threshold; applies to TSA-notified critical pipeline systems/facilities. |
| [PHMSA Control Room Management](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-192.631) | 49 CFR 192.631 (gas); 49 CFR 195.446 (hazardous liquid) | Reduced requirements for control rooms limited to distribution with < 250,000 services or transmission without a compressor station (192.631(a)(1)). |
| [CIRCIA (Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act of 2022) - proposed 6 CFR Part 226](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/04/04/2024-06526/cyber-incident-reporting-for-critical-infrastructure-act-circia-reporting-requirements) | 6 U.S.C. 681-681g; proposed 6 CFR Part 226 (NPRM 89 FR 23644, Apr. 4, 2024) | Proposed 226.2(a): exceeds SBA size standard in 13 CFR Part 121 for the entity's NAICS code (employee- or revenue-based depending on NAICS); sector-based criteria apply regardless of size. |

Whether each requirement applies at this size is decided at the start of P03, the gap analysis (build step 5).

| 2 | [P02 System Security Plan (SSP)](step-02_P02_system-security-plan/_context.md) | Core business system(s) run by the MSP and SaaS vendors. Standard SSP outline with inherited controls from MSP/SaaS noted. System: Pipeline SCADA and Gas Control System (PSGCS). | P05: which systems matter and how long they can be down |
| 3 | [P04 Control-to-Cloud Architecture Mapping](step-03_P04_cloud-control-mapping/_context.md) | SaaS plus any single cloud workload. Customer vs provider responsibility; MSP responsibilities called out. | P02: the system boundary and its controls |

Incident: Ransomware on Office IT Forcing a Precautionary Pipeline Shut-in. | P05 recovery order; P01 risks; P03 notification duties |

| 10 | [P10 AI Governance Risk Assessment](step-10_P10_ai-governance/_context.md) | One AI use case. Risk tier; data protection; human-in-the-loop decisions. AI use case: Pipeline leak-detection anomaly module. | P06 policies; the P01 risk method |
